Subject: Re: HorizonData security intake — deployment topology questions

Hi Steve,

Thanks again for the intake form — we reviewed your SIG request and wanted to confirm a few things before we produce the control crosswalk and evidence packet:

- You indicated a mix of cloud-hosted VPC (us-west-2) and an on-premise instance for certain regulated workloads. Can you confirm the list of services and data classes that will be pinned to on-prem? (example: PII/SSN ingestion from payment flows)
- For the hosted VPC workloads, does HorizonData require customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) or would customer-managed keys via our KMS integration be sufficient?
- Any specific retention/ingress egress controls for telemetry/LLM telemetry that differ between the two modes?

I've attached a draft control crosswalk (sig_control_crosswalk_v1.pdf) and a quick XLS with the proposed scope mapping (horizon_vpc_scope.xlsx).

If you can confirm the items above, we'll enumerate the precise artifacts and provide a prioritized delivery timeline (we typically split evidence into Phase A: management controls + KMS proof; Phase B: telemetry + deployment-level network proofs).

Next steps: if useful we can do a short 30-min tech sync tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT to walk the crosswalk.

Best,
Camila
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sig_control_crosswalk_v1.pdf (PDF stub), horizon_vpc_scope.xlsx (Excel stub)

From: Steve Huang <steve.h@horizondata.com>

Date: 2026-11-28T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HorizonData security intake — deployment topology questions

Thanks Camila — useful start. Quick clarifications inline: 

> - You indicated a mix of cloud-hosted VPC (us-west-2) and an on-premise instance for certain regulated workloads. Can you confirm the list of services and data classes that will be pinned to on-prem?

On-prem will host our payment reconciliation service (PaymentQ) and the ingestion pipeline for raw PII (names, SSNs, DOB). We will not host model weights on-prem; models will remain in the VPC.

> - For the hosted VPC workloads, does HorizonData require customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) or would customer-managed keys via our KMS integration be sufficient?

We require BYOK for production keys; test/dev can use managed keys.

> - Any specific retention/ingress egress controls for telemetry/LLM telemetry that differ between the two modes?

Telemetry that includes request-level identifiers tied to PII must not cross the on-prem boundary; aggregated telemetry is fine to flow to hosted analytics.

We can do a sync tomorrow — 10:00 PT works for Amira and me. Please include your infra lead.

--
Steve Huang
Head of InfoSec, HorizonData

Quick technical note from infra:

- BYOK: We support customer-supplied keys via our KMS connector (HSM-backed) for the production VPC namespace. We will provide: a rotation ledger extract (proof_kms_rotation.txt), a signed policy document (signed by infra lead), and a sample API call demonstrating key usage.
- On‑prem access: For the PaymentQ appliance we propose a scrubbing gateway. Remote maintenance will be by time-limited bastion sessions; all sessions recorded and stored in a redacted session store.
- Telemetry: We can partition telemetry at the ingestion layer so request-level identifiers with PII remain on-prem. Aggregated metrics (counts, latency histograms) flow to hosted analytics via a one-way push.

Requested evidence list (phase A/B):
A — Management and crypto proofs (within 7 business days): sig_control_crosswalk_v1.pdf, proof_kms_rotation.txt, rotation_ledger_export.csv (sample), signed-kms-policy.pdf
B — Deployment & telemetry proofs (within 15 business days): bastion-session-log-samples.tar.gz (redacted), network flow diagrams (VPC subnet ACLs), on-prem scrubbing-gateway config extract

We can demo the key rotation ledger live during the 30-min sync; that would probably clear most procurement questions.

-Vivek
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
